haiku-low.q1: Keys load before the server starts listening. /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys load, so the pod is not ready before then.
haiku-low.q2: The pod exits non-zero after its retries, never becomes ready, and the rollout halts. Old pods keep serving traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Refresh task re-reads each secret every 5 minutes, swapping it in on success. On failure, keeps last good value and logs a warning.
haiku-low.q4: Held in memory in the holder. Never written to disk, environment variables, logs, or exception messages.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod workload identity reads prod values; no engineer role can. Only the security on-call role writes them.
haiku-low.q6: Git history keeps the old keys, so they are not removed. They become harmless only when revoked at the provider in step 7.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider client reads its key from the holder on every request, rather than copying it in its constructor.
haiku-low.q8: Checks each pod's last log shows the recorded version id, no old-image pods, zero old-key requests at provider for 15 minutes, and no refresh warnings.
haiku-low.q9: Store access (step 2), new provider keys (3), store writes (4), app switch and config removal (5). Revocation of old keys follows at step 7.
haiku-low.q10: From orders-api/dev/* via each developer's own engineer identity. Never from prod or old live keys. How engineers log in is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: It retries, then logs the failing secret name and attempt count, never values, and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The plan sets no rotation schedule; security has not decided whether or how often keys rotate.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first. The pod reads all three secrets into the holder, then builds clients, and only then starts listening. /healthz answers 200 only after that, so readiness comes after the keys are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries (one attempt plus three retries, 2 seconds apart), logs the secret names and attempt count, and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rollout halts. With maxUnavailable: 0, old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background refresh task re-reads all three secrets every 5 minutes. Each secret is swapped in atomically and independently when its read succeeds. If a read fails, the pod keeps the last good value and logs one warning starting with 'secret refresh failed' (secret name, attempted version id, error class). Readiness is unchanged and the pod does not restart.
sonnet.q4: Keys are held in memory only, in the holder. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs. The document also lists exception messages, repr output, the Authorization header in HTTP debug logs, core dumps, and the store SDK's on-disk cache.
sonnet.q5: Read: only the orders-api-prod workload identity can read orders-api/prod/*. No engineer role can read it, and the policy simulator confirms that engineer and CI roles cannot. Write: only the security on-call role.
sonnet.q6: The old key values remain in git history, which is not rewritten. The old keys are harmless because all three are rotated and then revoked at the providers (step 7), after the gate in step 6 confirms nothing still uses them.
sonnet.q7: Each provider client reads its key from the holder on every request. It does not copy the key in its constructor. The refresh swaps the new value into the holder, so the next request uses it.
sonnet.q8: Step 6 gate, run at least 5 minutes after the last write. For each of the four prod pods, the latest startup or refresh log line for each key must show the version id recorded in the tracking issue. No pod may be on the pre-migration image. Other consumers in the inventory must use the new keys. Provider old-key requests must be zero for 15 minutes. There must be zero 'secret refresh failed' log matches in 15 minutes. The security on-call then signs off.
sonnet.q9: Order: 1 inventory and capability check; 2 set up store layout, KMS and access; 3 create new keys at providers (rotation); 4 validate and write the keys into the store, plus a read check; 5 release code that reads the store and remove the keys from config; 6 confirm gate; 7 revoke old keys; 8 verify the CI guard; 9 local development on dev keys.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store, orders-api/dev/*, using dev (sandbox or test) keys. Each developer uses their own engineer identity. make run and the tests use the same loader. Tests use an in-memory fake source instead. How engineers log in to the dev store is not settled (open question).
sonnet.q11: The document gives no separate handling for a single missing secret among reachable ones. By the general rule, if any secret still fails after one attempt plus three retries, it logs the secret names and attempt count and exits non-zero, so the pod never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: No. The plan sets no rotation schedule. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate, and that is an open question.
